This deletion results in a frameshift and a premature stop codon (p.D192TfsX49).

cases.statement: One person in the batch: the hemizygous male proband (II 2) of a Japanese family (19057086), who is also Family 9's proband in the 30413001 survey (merged; 30413001 cites 19057086 as reference [13]). His two affected heterozygous sisters are carriers not in the batch.

people.label: II 2
people.key_phenotypes: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from age 5 progressing to a dilated phase; mild skeletal myopathy; vacuoles with acetylcholinesterase activity on muscle biopsy; heart failure at 18; normal intelligence

quotes.quote: In the probands, a hemizygous c.573delA variant was identified in exon 5 of LAMP2 (Fig 5).
However, when he was 5 years old, he had been referred to another hospital because of heart murmur and was diagnosed as having obstructive HCM.
Echocardiography revealed marked LVH and progressive LV dilatation (Fig 3), a finding compatible with the dilated phase of HCM.
On examination, he had normal intelligence. Neurological examination revealed mild skeletal myopathy.
Acetylcholine and nonspecific esterase activities were associated with the vacuolar membranes (Figs 4C,D).

phenotype_specificity.statement: HCM with myopathy led the authors to Danon disease; muscle biopsy findings supported it. Acid maltase and alpha-galactosidase activities were normal (Pompe and Fabry disease considered). Sarcomere gene testing is not reported.

quotes.quote: Laboratory tests showed elevation of serum AST, ALT, LDH and aldolase, suggesting glycogen storage disease or Fabry disease, but the activity of both acid maltase and α-galactosidase was confirmed to be within the normal range.
The combined characteristics of HCM and myopathy led us to investigate Danon disease as the underlying etiology.
These findings supported the diagnosis of Danon disease.

segregation.statement: Two affected sisters are heterozygous (elder: abnormal ECG and mild LVH; younger: ECG suggestive of WPW and LVH). The father does not carry it. The affected mother (DCM, died at 43) was not tested. 30413001 Table 1 lists proband, mother and 2 sisters as affected for Family 9.

quotes.quote: Both of his sisters were heterozygous for this deletion (Fig 5), but his father did not carry the mutation.

His elder sister had abnormal ECGs and mild LVH on echocardiography, and the younger sister had electrocardiographic abnormalities suggestive of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, and LVH on echocardiography.
His mother died at the age of 43 years from advanced heart failure, 4 years after the onset of dilated cardiomyopathy.
DNA was not available from their deceased mother, but as this is an X-linked gene it is likely that the mother was a carrier.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo by the paper's account: the mother was untested (DNA unavailable) and presumed by the authors to be a carrier; the father does not carry it.

quotes.quote: Both of his sisters were heterozygous for this deletion (Fig 5), but his father did not carry the mutation.
DNA was not available from their deceased mother, but as this is an X-linked gene it is likely that the mother was a carrier.

functional.statement: No functional study of this variant was done; the authors say so explicitly.

quotes.quote: Functional analysis of the mutation found in the present family has not been performed, but frameshift mutations are likely to lead to the absence of functional protein (males) or haplo-insufficiency (females), as previously demonstrated.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: One-base deletion predicted to cause a frameshift (p.(Asp192ThrfsTer50) on the batch transcript; the paper writes p.D192TfsX49). The authors state it truncates LAMP-2 with loss of the transmembrane domain, and that frameshifts lead to absent protein in males and haploinsufficiency in females.

quotes.quote: This deletion results in a frameshift and a premature stop codon (p.D192TfsX49).

The novel mutation identified in this family is encoded in exon 5 and leads to premature truncation of LAMP-2 with abolition of the transmembrane domain, and thus can lead to an accumulation of autophagic vacuoles mainly in cardiac and skeletal muscle cells.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Cohort-level statement in 30413001: none of the survey's mutations was found in 100 Japanese controls. 19057086 gives no control data.

quotes.quote: On screening 100 Japanese controls, the same mutations were not found.

authors_classification.statement: No formal classification; the authors describe it as a novel frameshift mutation.

quotes.quote: The proband developed marked concentric hypertrophy at the age of 5 years and DNA analyses revealed a novel hemizygous frameshift mutation (c.573delA) in exon 5.

concerns: Protein notation differs in the stop position: paper p.D192TfsX49 vs batch p.(Asp192ThrfsTer50) (likely a counting convention difference; the panel should confirm).
Carriers missing from the batch: the two heterozygous affected sisters (elder sister labelled II 1) are not in the batch rows.
The proband's age is given as 17 in the case report and 18 in the abstract (heart failure emerged at 18).

30413001 contradicts itself on recurrent variants: the text says Family 11 and Family 15 share c.877C > T, while Table 1 lists c.877C>T for Families 10 and 14, c.371_372 delCA for Family 11 and c.56T>C for Family 15.
30413001 gives two different counts for families whose mothers or relatives tested negative (eight families in Results, 10 families in Discussion) and does not say which families these are.
notes_for_panel: Segregation in two heterozygous affected sisters; father negative; mother untested but affected (DCM).
